To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a hybrid methodology is proposed that integrates the UML with the FB model to semi automatically generate a design diagram in the IEC61499 FB model; and that a heuristic-based approach is proposed to assign instances of FBs to the execution environment of the distributed application, so as to meet temporal constraints.

the methodology is able to: (i) generate an executable control application, (ii) allocate the generated application on a network of devices, (iii) consider constraints of devices and of FB instances. 2
the methodology is based on the UML and FB models, it can be applied to the development and deployment phases of control applications, and it can be applied on a network of PLC devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a design methodology and a tool to support the development of distributed control applications based on the IEC61499 paradigm.
a methodology for the design and deployment of IEEC 61499-based distributed control applications.
a new approach for the development of IEC6149-based distributed control applications, where the FB model is combined with a hybrid UML approach to semi automatically generate a design diagram.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methodology presented here is an efficient and effective approach for the development of IEC614999-based control applications.
the proposed methodology can be considered as a feasible approach to develop IEC61499 applications on a networked distributed execution environment. 2 IEC 61499: The standard that never was.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a methodology for developing and deploying IEC61499 control applications on a distributed execution environment.
the proposed approach is capable of handling the development and deployment process for IEC61499 based distributed applications.
we are able to provide an approach to develop and deploy distributed control applications based on the IEC61499 model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed methodology can be used to design and implement IEC61499 applications on a networked execution environment, which can help to reduce development costs and improve the reliability of these applications.
the methodology is able to automatically generate a network of interconnected IEC61499 FBs that can be mapped to the execution environment.
the proposed approach can be used as a basis for developing tools for the design, development, and deployment of distributed industrial control applications based on the IEC61499 paradigm.
